strands.title: Art in life and uneven survival

strands.title: Play as a meaningful cultural activity
strands.focus: Huizinga examines absorption, voluntary activity and the shifting relation to seriousness; play is not reduced to leisure or a biological utility.

strands.title: Collective conditions and social psychology
strands.focus: Lamprecht’s program and reading of Herder differ from Burckhardt’s synthesis; his insistence on collective explanatory priority remains contested.

before.label: National & imperial narratives

before.representative_figures_and_works: A broad context of historical production, not one school: nation-building, colonial institutions, and resistance generate different and often conflicting projects.

after.label: National & imperial narratives
after.description: National and imperial histories join source work to competing accounts of peoples, states, liberty and civilization. Michelet, Macaulay and Bancroft differ in method and purpose; colonial hierarchies, liberation histories and critiques of nationalist exclusions remain in tension.

verification.note: Complete translator preface, I.1, II.1 and V.6 read in the Gutenberg transcription: printed pp. iii–iv, 3–7, 129–133 and 395–401. Preface identifies translation from third German edition with Geiger additions and Valbusa material; do not treat it as an unaltered 1860 witness. Endnotes and original German not collated. Supports political conditions, individuality, interpretive categories and the upper-class women equality argument criticized by Kelly. Claims of civilizational superiority, gender character and medieval uniformity remain Burckhardt’s contestable assertions.

verification.note: Complete April 1924 preface read; opening selections of chapters I (first 9500 characters), XIX and XXIII (first 5500 each) consulted. A clipped XIX passage was reread. Preface identifies author-directed adaptation, reduction and consolidation, not a complete translation of the Dutch editions. Cultural endings, formalized emotions, uneven survival of images/documents and overlapping medieval/classical forms are arguments, not established universal descriptions.
